we have prepared and characterized the first monomeric FeIV O complex in an aqueous solution and have shown by spectroscopic and computational methods that the complex has a high spin state (S = 1) and that the TAML ligand donates electron density to the iron center.
the FeIV O complex [Fe (IV) (O) B*](2-) was synthesized and characterized by Mössbauer, magnetic, and EXAFS spectroscopies and by DFT calculations.

the one-electron reduction product of the S = 1 complex [Fe (IV) (O)B*](2-) is a S = 2 species that exhibits a large zero-field splitting and is stabilized by hydrogen bonding of the Fe (IV) oxo group with solvent water molecules.

the synthesis and characterization of iron (III) and iron (IV) complexes of TAML ligands.

the Fe (IV) species is stabilized by the presence of a hydrogen-bonding donor in the first coordination shell.
